precision_angle_check.source: Example 56 uses degrees; Try 56 question 2 explicitly uses radians. Try 56 question 1 asks an unevaluated inverse expression, with 150° geometry.
precision_angle_check.comparison: Convert all angles before calculation. Do not subtract 30 degrees from a radian arctangent. Exact surd lengths are not rounded; p and x are strictly positive length scales.

subparts.method: In right triangle ADC, AD=p>0 and angle DAC=30°. Thus AC=p cos30°. The coordinate cross-check scales a unit triangle by positive p.
DC=p sin30°=p/2, and D is the midpoint of BC. Hence BC=2DC=p.
Pythagoras in ABC gives AB=p√[(cos30°)²+(2sin30°)²]. Pulling p outside the square root is justified by its positive length meaning, not an unrestricted real-symbol identity.

subparts.author_derivation: The whole acute angle BAC has tan(BAC)=BC/AC=2/√3. Since 30°<BAC<90°, the principal arctangent gives BAC, and x=BAC−30°. Independently use unit-p vectors AD=(√3/2,1/2) and AB=(√3/2,1): their normalized dot product is 5/(2√7). The stated acute angle difference has that same cosine, which uniquely determines x on (0°,90°).
subparts.method: Author mathematical reasoning from the original task; explicit source support/absence recorded. This logical comparison is not an automated proof.

subparts.method: A,B,X are collinear in that order, so angle CBX=180°−150°=30°. Its adjacent side BX=6cos30°=3√3 cm; CX=6sin30°=3 cm is an intermediate, not a separately asked answer.

subparts.author_derivation: The diagram fixes AX=AB+BX=4+3√3 and CX=3, so tan(CAB)=3/(4+3√3). CAB is acute, and its principal arctangent is therefore the requested angle. Retain the unevaluated inverse expression; the source does not request a numerical angle/unit.

Pythagoras in AXC gives AC²=(4+3√3)²+3²=52+24√3, and AC is the positive square root. As an independent route, the cosine rule in ABC with included angle 150° gives 4²+6²−2·4·6cos150°, the same squared length.

subparts.method: BM=MC=x>0 and angle ABC=π/3. First AC=2x tan(π/3)=2√3x. Then AM=x√[(2tan(π/3))²+1]=√13x. AC is an intermediate, not another requested output. The rendered key root bar covers 13 only, so it agrees.

subparts.author_derivation: Angle BAC=π/2−π/3=π/6. In right triangle ACM, angle MAC=atan(MC/AC)=atan(1/(2√3)), an acute principal value. Subtract MAC from BAC to get BAM=θ. Independent vectors from A to B and M have normalized dot product 7/(2√13), equal to the cosine of the stated positive acute difference.
